clue.text: Where Nash might have looked to meet Diogenes ? .

definitions.text: Where Nash might have looked to meet Diogenes ?

parts.words: Where Nash might have looked to meet Diogenes
parts.note: Beau Nash ruled society in the spa city of Bath, and Diogenes the Cynic famously lived in a tub, so the meeting place joins the two

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about where an English dandy might search for a Greek philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Nash was the eighteenth-century master of ceremonies at Bath, the Somerset spa town; Diogenes lived in a large jar or tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic bath vessel combines the dandy's city with the philosopher's famous dwelling.

clue.text: Block off

parts.note: read as an executioner's block, taking something off on it means removing the head

explanation.definitionFit: Execution on the block took off the head, so this is decapitation.

clue.text: I to camp in' Mexico for a change

indicators.note: making a change to the letters of the three words rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to go camping in Mexico for something different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges I TO CAMP into a Gulf coast port; the definition is the place's being 'in Mexico'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampico is a port city on Mexico's Gulf coast, so it lies within that country.

clue.text: Sceptical grunt in a court case-was that arch ?

indicators.note: the grunt is placed inside the court case, so the word in signals one piece within another

parts.note: a court case is a trial
umph, like humph, is a grunt of doubt

explanation.surface: Someone grunts in disbelief during a court case and wonders whether that was mischievous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' looks like the adjective meaning roguish, but it is the noun: a triumphal arch.
explanation.definitionFit: A victory arch built to celebrate a conqueror is called a triumphal one.

clue.text: What Kings Cross could lead to ?

definitions.text: What Kings Cross could lead to ?

parts.words: What Kings Cross could lead to
parts.note: not the London station but monarchs crossing one another, which could start a fight among royalty

explanation.surface: A question about where a London railway terminus might take you.
explanation.walkthrough: King's Cross is a major London railway station; here kings who are cross with each other fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all fight, literally a battle among royals.

clue.text: Shapers reshaped in heaven

indicators.note: the shapers are themselves reshaped, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Makers of things are made over in paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshaped' rearranges SHAPERS; the definition describes the angels by where they live.
explanation.definitionFit: Seraphim are the highest order of angels, dwelling in paradise.

clue.text: South of France for a bit of bubbly

explanation.surface: A trip to the Riviera for a glass of champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for south, and a single unit of soapsuds.

clue.text: He's right over that underground river

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sitting over another comes above it

parts.note: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's Kubla Khan that runs through caverns measureless to man

explanation.surface: A man is said to be just above a river running underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Alph comes from Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, so any man so called is a he.

clue.text: That's not to 'say Portsmouth got the ashes

indicators.note: to say signals a word spoken, so the city sounds like the naval town's nickname

parts.note: Pompey is the nickname of Portsmouth and its football club

explanation.surface: Portsmouth winning the cricket's Ashes, it seems, is not quite the claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got the ashes' suggests the cricket trophy, but means the volcanic ash of Vesuvius; 'That's not' warns the city only sounds like Pompey, Portsmouth's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman town buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: People of, promise

parts.note: godparents at a baptism make promises on a child's behalf, so they are people who pledge

explanation.definitionFit: Godparents who vouch for a child at baptism, or backers who guarantee support.

clue.text: Clumsy as a pork butcher on occasion

definitions.text: as a pork butcher on occasion
definitions.meaning: literally, with a fist full of cured pig's leg

explanation.surface: A clumsy pork butcher on a bad day.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward with the hands, and literally clutching cured pork in the fist.

clue.text: Look around-one medico offers oblivion here

indicators.note: the exclamation goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look
I is the Roman numeral one
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor glances about and offers forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of neglect or being forgotten, the theological borderland of the forgotten.

clue.text: Man 'is after a kiss-that's self-evident

indicators.note: the island's letters come after the others, so this phrase orders the charade

parts.note: X is the cross written for a kiss
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man is obviously after a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' reads as a person but is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea, abbreviated IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a principle accepted without proof as obviously true.

clue.text: They symbolize the freedom of the majority

definitions.text: They symbolize the freedom of the majority

parts.words: They symbolize the freedom of the majority
parts.note: reaching the age of majority traditionally meant being given your own door key to come and go freely

explanation.definitionFit: Front-door keys, traditionally given to someone come of age as a sign of independence.

clue.text: Vain repetition, in a word, involves ma's guilt too

indicators.note: involve once meant to entangle or wind together, so these letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: In a word, needless repetition brings in a mother's guilt as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' rearranges MASGUILTTOO; 'in a word' is a link, since the answer is a single word for saying the same thing twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless saying of the same thing twice in other words.

clue.text: They were carriers, now dispatchers

parts.note: ex means former, what something once was
porters carry luggage

explanation.surface: Former luggage carriers have become shippers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as ex-porters: people who were carriers.
explanation.definitionFit: People or firms that send goods abroad are dispatchers of trade.

clue.text: Key issue

parts.note: an ash key is the winged seed of the ash tree, and its issue, what grows from it, is a young tree

explanation.definitionFit: A young ash sapling, grown from the winged seed, also made into a walking stick.

clue.text: Brontë blooms?

parts.note: flowers named as if from Charlotte Brontë's novel about a heroine of that name

explanation.definitionFit: Red field flowers of a garden strain bred at a vicarage of that name, sharing the Brontë novel's title.

clue.text: Jacob has ' one for the National

parts.note: Jacob was renamed in Genesis after wrestling with the angel
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Jacob has a single entry for the national team.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Jacob is given the name by which his descendants' nation is known.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the Jewish state is one of its nationals.

clue.text: Dickensian star of the East ?

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east
stella is Latin for star

explanation.surface: A Dickens character is the star from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star of the East' recalls the Magi's star.
explanation.definitionFit: Pip's cold beloved in Great Expectations is a Dickens character.

clue.text: Edges old official in Messina

definitions.meaning: borders or margins, as of a road
the bumbling headborough, a constable's deputy, in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing, set in Messina

explanation.surface: An old official in the Sicilian port is on the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass borders of roads, and Dogberry's partner in Shakespeare's Sicilian comedy.

clue.text: Ministerial wine list

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
a folio is a leaf or page, here a written list

explanation.surface: A wine list fit for a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: A government minister's area of responsibility is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's office or department is a government brief.

clue.text: It'll be the end of Albert if he doesn't slim

parts.note: a man who fails to lose weight stays fat
Al is short for Albert

explanation.surface: A warning that Albert's weight will kill him unless he diets.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deadly is literally the end of you.

clue.text: Vicar of Wakefield so early riser? so says milton

definitions.text: Vicar of Wakefield so early riser? so says milton

parts.words: Vicar of Wakefield so early riser? so says milton
parts.note: Goldsmith's vicar is Dr Primrose, and Milton's Lycidas speaks of the early-blooming primrose with this old word for early

explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for early, used by Milton of the primrose, Goldsmith's vicar's surname.

clue.text: Concerning one Scots biblical testament

parts.note: ane is the Scots word for one
NT is the abbreviation for the New Testament

explanation.surface: Something about a Scottish copy of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: An old, chiefly Scots preposition meaning about or regarding.

clue.text: Iris: you look so pale-give up: with this?

parts.note: a very pale face is white
flag is another name for the iris plant

explanation.surface: Someone tells Iris she looks so pale she should surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a woman's name but is the plant, also called a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrender is signalled by waving a pale banner.

clue.text: Sydney Smith for instance gives point to it

parts.note: W, west, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A clergyman humorist adds sharpness to something.
explanation.walkthrough: Sydney Smith was a famously humorous English clergyman and essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever, funny person, as the epigrammatic clergyman was.

clue.text: Three hired by a poet

parts.note: a trio is a group of three
let means rented out

explanation.surface: Three people are taken on by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names the thing by its maker: something written by a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A short eight-line verse form, the kind of poem a poet writes.

clue.text: Grapes attract a mouse to its killers

parts.note: Mus is the Latin name, and genus, of the mouse
cats kill mice

explanation.surface: Grapes lure a mouse towards the cats that will kill it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet musky grape varieties used for wine and raisins.
